Evidence: Source 2 states that three doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine in children aged 6 months to under 5 years demonstrated a vaccine efficacy of 80.3% against symptomatic COVID-19. Source 3 indicates that the original Pfizer vaccine provided 33% protection against emergency department visits for children under 5 during the Omicron variant predominance. Source 1 mentions that while no vaccine is 100% effective, the benefits significantly outweigh potential risks, implying that vaccination does provide some level of protection.
Justification: The retrieved evidence from Source 2 indicates that three doses of the Pfizer vaccine provide an efficacy of 80.3% in children under 5, contradicting the claim that three doses do not protect this age group. Additionally, Source 3 shows that the vaccine offers 33% protection against urgent care visits, further supporting that vaccination does confer some level of protection, thus refuting the claim.
